session.title: 1.0.44 released: coding-plan presets for Z.ai, MiniMax, Kimi, Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud, BytePlus, OpenCode Go and Command Code
session.purpose: SW308 from a worker brief: research the international subscription coding plans of Z.ai, MiniMax, Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud, BytePlus and Kimi, DeepSeek's API, OpenCode Go and Command Code; add each existing plan as a preset in the tool it belongs to, with a usage badge where the plan's key exposes quota; no sign-ups. Then, at the user's instruction, publish 1.0.44 the way 1.0.43 was published and hand off.
outcomes: Research (README section 'Coding plans' holds the table, prices, keys and terms): every plan exists on its international service. Z.ai GLM Coding Plan, MiniMax M Plan (Token Plan closed to new buyers), Kimi Code membership on kimi.ai (kimi.ai is international, kimi.com and api.kimi.com are mainland), Alibaba Cloud Token Plan and Coding Plan Pro (Singapore), Tencent Cloud Token Plan Personal (Singapore), BytePlus ModelArk Coding Plan, OpenCode Go, Command Code (API on GOAT and up; the $1 Go plan is CLI-only). DeepSeek has no plan. No plan is restricted to its provider's own tools and none needs a mainland account or phone; OpenCode Go's and Command Code's terms forbid one person holding several accounts.

Built: Claude Code presets for all eight plans (international hosts, models from each provider's own Claude Code guide), OpenCode presets for Z.ai, MiniMax, Kimi, OpenCode Go and Command Code; OpenCode Go and Command Code are presets, not tabs (both are API keys; Command Code's cmdc CLI is not switched). A card from the Z.ai, MiniMax, Kimi or Command Code preset starts with the plan-quota badge on; Alibaba, Tencent and BytePlus expose quota only to a console login or signed cloud keys, and OpenCode Go's usage call needs a workspace id. DeepSeek's preset got its current models.

Existing Token Plan code: Kimi queried mainland api.kimi.com in the pre-2026-09 format (now api.kimi.ai and the used_ratio format, old one kept); MiniMax international queried a console endpoint that needs a login (now the documented /v1/token_plan/remains); Z.ai was international but showed its weekly pool as a second 5-hour one and missed refused keys answered with HTTP 200. An empty key now fails with 'No API key'; the badge shows Loading while its first reading is in flight.

Kimi Code tab: the Official template signs in on kimi.ai (OAuth slot oauth/kimi-code-env-0e4f99c69cc27850, oauthHost https://auth.kimi.ai) and the login file is the one the config's managed oauth key names, so kimi.ai logins switch. Claude switches now own CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS (DECISION_LOG 2026-10-25).

Checks: pnpm typecheck and the frontend tests pass (169 in the full run, plus the new badge test run on its own); cargo test passes except the proxy test that cannot bind 15721 while the installed Switchy holds it (README). Installed 1.0.44 on the workstation: every preset is on its tab with its international endpoint; a card made from a preset starts with its badge on; badges answer 'No API key' without a key and a clean authentication failure for sk-invalid-test from each live endpoint; on screen the failure arrived before the Loading state could be captured, which a component test covers. Test cards deleted.

Released 1.0.44 like 1.0.43: private origin pushed, public copy via scripts/publish_public.sh, macOS DMG from build-macos.yml on the public repo, GitHub release v1.0.44 (Latest) with the exe, msi and DMG. SW308 done with ref c8fc1e04; worker brief in brief_archive/. README's earlier 'Claude locked on registered2nd' line was stale (account_locks empty) and is corrected.

current_focus.summary: Switchy 1.0.44 is released (GitHub Latest, Windows installers and Apple Silicon DMG) and runs on the workstation: presets for the international coding plans of Z.ai, MiniMax, Kimi, Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud, BytePlus, OpenCode Go and Command Code (README section 'Coding plans'), with plan-quota badges for Z.ai, MiniMax, Kimi and Command Code, and Kimi Code cards signing in on kimi.ai. the user subscribes to the plans himself. The laptop has 1.0.40 with Switchy quit; another user's PC and Mac have 1.0.39. Await the user's feedback; the confirmations below stay pending under their triggers.

next_actions.summary: CONFIRM THE CRASH RESTART ON THE NEXT REAL CRASH (1.0.40). After any Switchy crash on the workstation: Application log event 1000 for switchy.exe, then within about a minute a new switchy.log starting with '[crash_restart] Windows will restart Switchy after a crash or hang' and the proxy on 15721 without a manual start; switchy.prev.log ends at the crash; ~/.switchy/crash.log gains an [ABNORMAL EXIT] entry naming the exception, any 'Windows ran out of memory' line and the dump path. A restart that did not happen while commit was still exhausted is the known single-attempt limit (finding doc option 2 is the backstop).

Confirm account-proxy coverage on the next natural Claude sign-in or renewal while Owen is selected, without forcing a new login. Claude Code's own exchange should log '[connect_tunnel] platform.claude.com:443 via socks5://82.26.163.142:45001'. For Switchy's renewal, observe '[claude_pool] refreshing login for provider=98e00f12...' and the successful refreshed-login message; the enforced per-account client route is owned by proxy/http_client.rs. Windows/WSL HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY, UK exit probes and telemetry tunnels were verified; a live sign-in/renewal using this route remains unobserved. Connection failures must stop rather than fall back to direct; country observations only warn.

CONFIRM THE RESTART PATH ON STEPHEN'S NEXT WINDOWS RESTART (1.0.29). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.prev.log after 'Session ending; handing the live configs back': '[session-end] claude/codex/gemini handed back', '[session-end] ... in WSL handed back', then 'Live configs handed back for the session end'. 'did not finish in 4 seconds' with the last [session-end] line shows which step stalls (Windows step = database lock, WSL step = WSL I/O); fix that step. In switchy.log: Switchy started within seconds of login (window hidden, launched with --autostart from HKCU Run), '[auto_launch] start at login on', proxy on 15721, and Claude Code / Codex answer without ECONNREFUSED.

CONFIRM CLAUDE LOGINS STAY IN STEP WITH WSL (1.0.27). In switchy.log, when an account WSL is signed in to renews: '[claude_pool] provider=... took the newer login from WSL' or 'wrote the refreshed login through to WSL', and no new 'invalid_grant' 'Refresh token not found or invalid' in account_switches/provider_health. WSL's ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.switchy/accounts/<id>/credentials.json for that account should carry the same refreshToken after each renewal.

CONFIRM ROTATION AND CODEX FAILOVER ON LIVE TRAFFIC (1.0.25/1.0.26). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log and the switchy.db account_switches table: (a) when an account's five-hour window resets while another serves, a switch back to it with reason 'recovered' and detail "Another account's weekly limit resets sooner"; (b) a Codex turn refused for usage that continues an earlier one logs '[CodexWS] provider=... websocket closed (turn refused for usage; Codex resends it in full)' and the turn then completes on the next account with no error in Codex. GET http://127.0.0.1:15721/switchy/accounts shows current account, pool order, quota and atLimit per account.

VERIFY LOCAL PROXY OFF WITH AN OPEN CODEX WINDOW. the user was asked to turn Local proxy off in Settings > Pool, then use a Codex window opened while the proxy was on. Confirm in C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log that "Proxy turned off; its listener stays up..." was logged, that the Codex window's later [Codex] requests still reached the proxy and answered, that netstat shows 127.0.0.1:15721 still LISTENING, and that Settings shows the proxy as off. Turning it back on must reuse the listener.

QUIT CASE WAITS ON STEPHEN. Quitting Switchy still breaks Codex windows opened under the proxy. He was offered a warning on quit naming the open Codex windows (small) or running the proxy as a process that outlives Switchy's window (large); he has not chosen. Build nothing until he does.
If the user directs request logging to be enabled, first make the Usage page's Turn on button apply to the running proxy, then enable it for Claude, Codex, and Gemini.

CONFIRM CURSOR/ANTIGRAVITY ON THE NEXT REAL SIGN-IN (1.0.43). No sign-in was run to test, and only one account of each exists. When the user adds a second account: enable the new empty card, open a NEW PowerShell, sign in. Expect: cursor-agent login prints 'Open a browser and navigate to this link' and opens no browser (user env NO_OPEN_BROWSER=1); agy started signed out shows its link with a code field and opens no browser (the profile function from ~/.switchy/manual_sign_in/agy_sign_in.ps1 sets SSH_CLIENT only when cmdkey lists no gemini:antigravity entry). Then switch back to the first card: switchy.log shows no '[cursor_account]'/'[antigravity_account] live login (...) is not the account' refusal for a normal switch, cursor-agent status and agy's log name the first account, and each card keeps its own email and usage badge ('[...] usage of provider=... N windows' lines). Kimi Code still opens the default browser (README limitation).

CONFIRM CODING-PLAN CARDS ON THE FIRST REAL KEY (1.0.44, SW308). No plan was subscribed; presets and badges were checked only against missing and invalid keys. When the user adds a plan card with a real key (preset from README section 'Coding plans', Claude Code or OpenCode tab): Claude Code answers on the preset's models, and the badge shows the plan's windows - Z.ai 5-hour and weekly (plan level in the hover), MiniMax 5-hour and weekly, Kimi 5-hour, weekly and monthly, Command Code 5-hour and weekly. 'Query failed' with a parse or missing-field error means the unpublished endpoint changed. Kimi Code tab: enable a new Kimi Code card, run kimi login and sign in on kimi.ai; ~/.kimi-code/credentials/kimi-code-env-0e4f99c69cc27850.json appears, and switching to another card and back restores that login.
